In Central America, at least 60 institutions in seven countries hold active zoological,…","status":"APPROVED","start":"2026-09-02","end":"2028-08-31","fundsAllocated":90000,"primaryLink":null,"programme":{"__typename":"Programme","fundingOrganisations":[{"id":"82242","title":"European Union","url":"http://europa.eu","logo":{"title":"European Union","file":{"url":"//images.ctfassets.net/uo17ejk9rkwj/6DO53L2kCckOgSKiyoU28i/73ce7be12fe8c9e90dd4c2516db099b7/flag-yellow-low.jpg"}},"__typename":"FundingOrganisation"}],"id":"82243","title":"BID: Biodiversity Information for Development"},"overrideProgrammeFunding":null,"projectId":"BID-REG2025-081","body":"

Scientific collections are indispensable for documenting and preserving reliable biodiversity information. In Central America, at least 60 institutions in seven countries hold active zoological, botanical and paleontological collections. However, only ten publishers in four countries are sharing collection data to GBIF (noting no fossil records are currently shared). Costa Rica and Guatemala have contributed 96 per cent of the available specimen records on GBIF from the region, but three countries, including El Salvador, have not yet mobilized collections to GBIF.

Following the priorities established in the 2026 BID Latin America and the Caribbean engagement meeting and Targets 20-21 outlined in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, this project strengthens the collaboration between institutions in Central America by facilitating mentorship from experienced participants to build and sustain regional capacity for collection data mobilization and use (integrating FAIR and CARE principles). This is achieved through expanding the GBIF network in the region.

Based on the successful model designed for the Guatemalan collections (comprised of four GBIF publishers, more than 25 collections, 50,000 occurrences and 18,000 images), a customized Symbiota portal will be activated to enable and sustain digitization, management and mobilization of Central American collections to GBIF. During the first year of the project, a series of tailored webinars and open sessions will be facilitated to mobilize 25 new collections (targeting Guatemala, El Salvador and Costa Rica), and review of quality data for more than 40 existing collection datasets. A hybrid meeting in Costa Rica aims to allow partners to interact, share preliminary results and participate in data use training for research and policy making, including validation of 33 checklist datasets.

By the end of the project, the consolidation of a Central American Network of Digitized Collections will promote continued collaboration and regional network growth.
